question: A 57-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-year history of fatigue, worsening shortness of breath, and a productive cough for 2 years. He has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 40 years. Examination shows pursed-lip breathing and an increased anteroposterior chest diameter. There is diffuse wheezing bilaterally and breath sounds are distant. Which of the following parameters is most likely to be decreased in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Smoking -> Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) -> Decreased lung elastic recoil -> 80% CHAIN: COPD -> Increased airway resistance -> Decreased lower airway resistance -> 70% CHAIN: COPD -> Emphysema -> Decreased thickness of small airways -> 60% CHAIN: COPD -> Chronic bronchitis -> Increased work of breathing -> 50% CHAIN: COPD -> Pulmonary hypertension -> Increased pulmonary vascular pressure -> 80%
analysis: Based on the patient's history and examination findings of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) likely due to smoking, the most likely parameter to be decreased in this patient is lung elastic recoil.
